Samantha 

2 thanks for the details and the diagram. Answers inline and a short technical plan below.

Inline answers:
1) Latency measurement: Redwood reports both "model-host latency" (time between request arrival at host and last token generated) and "edge-to-client latency" (time including our egress + customer network round-trip when we control the client). For private VPC, we can instrument end-to-end latency by running a lightweight probe in your VPC that measures time from client send to first token arrival back at probe. We'll include both numbers in the SLO table.
2) MTU/keep-alive: For long-lived token streaming (HTTP/2 or gRPC streaming), we recommend setting TCP keep-alive to 60s and ensuring path MTU >= 1400. If your NGFW fragments packets below that, small token chunks can add jitter. We'll include an MTU checklist in the POC doc.

Technical POC plan (2 weeks):
- Week 0: Pre-kickoff: exchange IPs, create test user, and set up VPN/peering flow.
- Week 1: Baseline tests (single-client streaming latency, 1-4 concurrency stress tests). Collect model-host and end-to-end metrics.
- Week 2: Scale tests (concurrency up to 8, throughput ramp to 500 req/min), failover and NAT behavior validation, and error-rate / QoS observations.

Preliminary notes based on your diagram:
- Because egress goes through NGFW with SNAT, we'll need a small port pool documented for the VPN endpoint to avoid ephemeral port exhaustion under high concurrency.
- If your transit path has a hi-latency hop (we saw a 12-15ms hop in the traceroute), that consumes most of the internal latency budget; we should consider regional peering in us-west-2 to reduce hops.
